explanations.supply: The main switch disconnects the home's supply. The distribution board divides that supply into separate circuits.
explanations.breaker: An MCB cuts off a circuit if too much current flows. Fix the fault before resetting it.
explanations.earth: The earth wire provides a path for fault current so a protective device can disconnect the supply. Never disconnect it to keep an appliance running.
explanations.radial: A radial circuit goes from the distribution board to each point and ends at the last one.
explanations.ring: A ring circuit returns to the same breaker it started from. Current can reach the sockets along two paths.
explanations.continuity: A continuity test checks whether a wire has an unbroken path from one end to the other. Isolate the supply before testing.
explanations.insulation: Insulation keeps electricity inside the wires. A high insulation resistance helps show that current is not leaking between them.

LR-02.ownTracking: This is for your own tracking.
LR-02.loopLine: Read this lesson again, then practise the questions you missed.

1: Electricity can hurt or kill you. Always switch off the supply and lock it before you start work.
Wear the right personal protective equipment (PPE). This means insulated gloves, safety shoes and eye protection.
Test the circuit with a tester before you touch it. Never trust a switch alone.
2: Ohm's law links voltage, current and resistance. Voltage equals current times resistance: V = I × R.
If the resistance stays the same and the voltage goes up, the current goes up too.
Use this to check a circuit. If you know the voltage and the resistance, you can work out the current.
3: Earthing connects the metal body of an appliance to the ground with a wire. This wire gives electricity a safe path to the earth.
If a live wire touches the metal body, a fault current flows. It takes the earth path because that path has very low resistance.
This large current makes the MCB or fuse operate. The supply switches off quickly, so nobody gets a shock from the metal body.
4: An MCB switches off the circuit when the current is too high. You can switch it on again after you fix the fault.
A fuse does the same job, but its wire melts. You must replace the fuse after it blows.
An RCCB watches for current leaking to earth. It switches off fast and protects people from electric shock.
5: This lesson is the checkpoint quiz for this course.
Read your earlier lessons before you start.
Take the quiz from the Quizzes page when you are ready.
